title: Weekly seat planner with skill levels and hour budgets
scenario: Open projects are staffed highest priority number first; each seat goes to the eligible contributor with the best skill level, then most hours left. The report lists unfilled seats, skill gaps over open projects, and utilisation.

verified.why_correct: Sorting by `-p.priority` looks like a flipped sort, but this README says the higher number is more important, so descending is right; ties go to the lower id and only open projects are kept.

bugs.title: Status check always truthy
bugs.symptom: Test 1 test_1_emea_projects: PR-01 is ['E-03', 'E-01', 'E-02'] and PR-02 is ['E-03', 'E-01'] instead of ['E-01', 'E-02'] for both. The paused E-03 is staffed.
bugs.why: This parses as `(status == 'active') or 'trial'`, and the non-empty string 'trial' is truthy, so every status passes. Paused E-03 (python 9) takes the top seat on PR-01 and PR-02.
hints: E-03 is staffed. Check E-03's status.
Look at how is_available decides eligibility.
`status == 'active' or 'trial'` is always truthy; use `status in ELIGIBLE_STATUSES`.
probes: Why didn't offboarded A-04 show up in any assignment?
What does `bool('active' == 'paused' or 'trial')` evaluate to, and why?

bugs.title: skill_level gives up after the first skill
bugs.symptom: Test 1 test_2_apac_projects: PR-03 is ['P-02', 'P-03'] instead of ['P-01', 'P-02']. P-01's sql:9 is not seen.
bugs.why: With `return 0` inside the loop, only a contributor's first listed skill is ever checked. P-01 lists python before sql, so their sql level 9 reads as 0 and P-03 takes the seat instead.
hints: P-01 has sql:9 but wasn't staffed on PR-03. What is different about how P-01's skills are written?
The `return 0` is indented inside the for loop; dedent it so it runs after the loop.
probes: Why were the Americas projects unaffected even though A-01 and A-05 also list two skills?
How would you write a test that catches this directly?

bugs.title: Skill gaps count on-hold projects
bugs.symptom: Test 2 test_3_skill_gaps_for_americas_skills: spanish shows 3 unfilled seats instead of 0 (math is still 1).
bugs.why: `unfilled` is computed for every project, including on-hold ones that are never staffed, so iterating all projects adds PR-07's three spanish seats (and PR-09/PR-10) to the gaps. The spec counts open projects only.
hints: Spanish shows 3 missing seats but every open spanish seat is filled. Where do 3 seats come from?
Which projects does skill_gaps loop over?
Loop over project_order(projects) (open projects only), not every project.
probes: Why doesn't the `unfilled` section show PR-07 even though skill_gaps counts it?
Why did this not raise a KeyError for on-hold projects?

context_qa.q: How does staff() pick each seat?
context_qa.a: For each project from project_order it loops until the seats are filled: it builds a pool of contributors not already picked for this project who pass `can_take`, and takes the `min` by `(-skill_level, -remaining, id)`. The winner's hours_used goes up by hours_per_seat.
A list of (name, level) tuples in written order: [('math', 6), ('spanish', 1)]. Blank parts are skipped and names are lower-cased.
`is_available(contributor)`, region equal to the contributor's or 'any', `skill_level(contributor, project.skill) >= project.min_level`, and `remaining >= hours_per_seat`, combined with `and`.
In build_report, for every project in projects.csv: seats minus the number of ids in `assignments.get(project_id, [])`. The report's `unfilled` section is then limited to the ids in `assignments`.
Those for which `is_available` is truthy and weekly_hours is non-zero, sorted by id, with hours_used / weekly_hours rounded to 2 decimals.
Computed: a property returning weekly_hours - hours_used, so it reflects seats already taken earlier in the run.
